content: Node.js TZ behavior: since Node 13, assigning process.env.TZ at runtime IS reflected in new Date() on Linux (glibc) — verified community examples (SO 77014077, jest#9856 'Node.js 13+ allows setting process.env.TZ and having it affect new Dates at runtime'); cache-clearing is libc-dependent (nodejs/node#11586: works with musl, glibc behavior noted) and TZ is unreliable on Windows (node#31478 wontfix). Jest historically ignored in-test TZ changes (jest#9856) because it caches — the safe pattern for any runner is setting TZ on the process before the suite starts. For Breeze this matters only for test invocation strategy: run the vitest suite twice (TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Kolkata) rather than mutating TZ inside tests; and design @breeze/core on explicit utcOffsetSeconds wall-clock arithmetic so correctness doesn't depend on host TZ at all.
